subject: Clarifying penetration-test boundaries across deployment modes
messages:
From: Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@crescentbio.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@redwoodsec.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: penetration test report + scope for procurement

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Procurement at Crescent needs the most recent penetration test materials and a clear statement of which deployment models are covered (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private/VPC, On-prem). The legal team also asked for any redacted findings and a remediation status overview.

We have a Pilot reserved under CRB-5412 and need to confirm whether the Dedicated pilot environment is included in your existing pentest reports or will require a separate engagement. Attached is the signed NDA for reference (Crescent_NDA_signed.pdf).

Can you confirm:
- Which of your hosting modes are included in the standard penetration test?
- If a Dedicated instance is in-scope by default or requires an explicit add-on/scope change?
- Timeline to get a redacted report and remediation summary?

Appreciate a short reply — procurement wants to close the packet this week.

Thanks,
Elena Vasquez
Director, IT Security
Crescent Biotech

--
Attachment: Crescent_NDA_signed.pdf (application/pdf, 147KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@crescentbio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report + scope for procurement

Elena — thanks for the note and the NDA. Quick summary up front, then details below.

Summary:
- Hosted API (shared hosted runtime): we run annual third-party penetration tests and can provide a redacted executive summary and remediation status. Full reports are redacted for customer confidentiality.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated pools): included in our standard PT coverage when customers are on Redwood Dedicated and the deployment uses our managed network/equipment. If you deploy Dedicated into a customer-provisioned network segment, scope may change — we can confirm for the CRB-5412 pilot.
- Private / VPC (control plane managed by Redwood but network peering to customer VPC): we provide a scoped set of tests covering our control plane components we manage. The customer-side VPC and their managed infra are out of scope.
- On-prem (customer-managed on-prem package): out of scope for Redwood's penetration test; we provide a package of hardening guidance, runbooks, and a customer-run test checklist.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attach the current infra boundary diagram for Hosted/Dedicated/Private (redwood_infra_boundary_v2.pdf).
2) Monica (cc'd) can confirm whether the CRB-5412 Dedicated pilot is on a Redwood-managed pool (if you share the environment id).
3) If you need a complete unredacted report for legal review, we'll need an executed mutual NDA (we have yours) and a formal request from Crescent legal — we can then assess sharing options.

Additional detail below.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@crescentbio.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report + scope for procurement

Elena / team — looping in ops/security to give official guidance for procurement. A few clarifications and what we can provide today.

Official scope stance:
- Hosted API: included in our quarterly/annual third-party assessments. We can provide a redacted PDF executive summary and a table of remediation status (see attached pt_finding_summary_Q3_2027.pdf). We do not expose tenant-level production data or customer-specific internal network tests for security/privacy reasons.
- Redwood Dedicated (managed pools): When Dedicated is provisioned on our managed infrastructure (Redwood is the operator of the GPU hosts, network, and control plane), that environment is covered by our PT program and by SOC 2 evidence. For pilot Dedicated environments that run on our managed fleet, we can confirm they are covered retrospectively if the environment was included in the engagement window — otherwise we can schedule a targeted assessment.
- Private / VPC (control plane or managed control plane with VPC peering): Our penetration testing covers the Redwood-managed components (control plane, runtime services we operate). Customer VPC resources (subnets, customer-managed services) are out of scope; we supply a checklist to support customer-side testing and recommended segmentation.
- On-prem/offline package: This is explicitly out of scope. For on-prem customers we provide a standard hardening guide and an artefact package (runbooks, baselines) and can support a customer-conducted penetration test by providing scope documents.

Remediation status:
- High/critical items from Q3-2027 have been closed or mitigated; medium items have scheduled remediations (ETA listed in the attachment). We will provide a redacted remediation table for procurement.

Sharing controls and process:
- Redacted executive reports can be shared after an NDA (we've received Crescent's copy).
- For Dedicated unredacted reports or targeted add-on assessments, we require a short SOW and an approval from Redwood Security (standard procurement flow).

Monica — can you confirm the provisioning type for CRB-5412 (Redwood-managed Dedicated pool vs customer-managed)? Rishi / Security will prepare the redacted PT executive summary and remediation table once we confirm scope.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

--

Laura — thanks, that helps a lot. We are aiming to include the redacted executive report in the packet for senior procurement review tomorrow. Two quick follow-ups:
1) Can you confirm an expected delivery timeframe for the redacted executive summary + remediation table? We would need it by 2028-04-05 COB if possible.
2) For CRB-5412: the pilot was provisioned via your Sales onboarding ticket (see HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/CRB-5412). My technical contact says the pilot was created on a Redwood-managed Dedicated pool — please confirm so we can note it as in-scope.

If you can confirm both items in the next 24 hours that would unblock procurement.

Best,
Elena
